item.research_question: Can a medium-entropy alloy with a single-phase face-centered cubic structure be strengthened by introducing hierarchical ordered phases via a two-step annealing process?
item.processing_route: Vacuum induction melting, multi-directional forging, homogenization at 1150°C, cold rolling, recrystallization annealing at 750°C, and aging at 650°C
item.test_conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with a constant strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
key_findings: The tri-phase alloy exhibits an ultrahigh tensile strength exceeding 1.6 GPa
The alloy maintains an exceptional ductility of 30% at room temperature
The simultaneous activation of unusual dislocation multiple slip and stacking faults in the κ phase contributes to enhanced strain hardening and excellent ductility
The introduction of V element in the fcc matrix induces severe lattice distortion, improving the effectiveness of solid solution strengthening
The strengthening effect of κ phase is comparable to the high concentration of vanadium in the equimolar CoNiV MEA
The unique multiple deformation mechanisms contribute to extraordinary strain hardening ability and ductility
item.mechanism: The strengthening effect of the hierarchical ordered phases, including grain refinement, second-phase strengthening, and solid solution strengthening, contributes to the enhanced strength and ductility of the alloy
quotes: Ultrastrong and ductile medium-entropy alloys via hierarchical ordering
A strategy to defeat the strength-ductility paradox by two-stage ordered phases was presented

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a medium-entropy alloy with a single-phase face-centered cubic structure be strengthened by introducing hierarchical ordered phases via a two-step annealing process?. System: Ni2CoFeV medium-entropy alloy. Processing: Vacuum induction melting, multi-directional forging, homogenization at 1150°C, cold rolling, recrystallization annealing at 750°C, and aging at 650°C. Test conditions: Tensile testing at room temperature with a constant strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1. Findings: The tri-phase alloy exhibits an ultrahigh tensile strength exceeding 1.6 GPa; The alloy maintains an exceptional ductility of 30% at room temperature; The simultaneous activation of unusual dislocation multiple slip and stacking faults in the κ phase contributes to enhanced strain hardening and excellent ductility; The introduction of V element in the fcc matrix induces severe lattice distortion, improving the effectiveness of solid solution strengthening; The strengthening effect of κ phase is comparable to the high concentration of vanadium in the equimolar CoNiV MEA; The unique multiple deformation mechanisms contribute to extraordinary strain hardening ability and ductility. Mechanism: The strengthening effect of the hierarchical ordered phases, including grain refinement, second-phase strengthening, and solid solution strengthening, contributes to the enhanced strength and ductility of the alloy. Quote: "Ultrastrong and ductile medium-entropy alloys via hierarchical ordering"
